data.long_meaning: Jagat (world) + Pal (protector). Jagpal is a Sanskrit name that means 'Lord of the World' or 'Protector of the World'. This name is derived from the Sanskrit words jagat (world) and pal (protector). It is a powerful and spiritual name that represents strength, protection, and leadership. The name Jagpal carries the meaning “Lord of the World” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jagpal usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the world and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: The Indian subcontinent gained independence from British rule in 1947. Jagpal Singh was the last ruler of the princely state of Nabha, which was one of the many small states comprising British India. After India's independence, these princely states were integrated into the Indian Union. Jagpal Singh ruled from 1942 to 1948.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Jagpal Singh Ranjit Singh was a prominent Sikh military leader in the late 19th century. The name Jagpal carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Ranjit Singh was the Maharaja of the Sikh Empire from 1839 to 1849. Jagpal Singh Ranjit Singh was one of his most trusted generals and played a key role in several military campaigns. He is particularly noted for his victory in the Battle of Gujrat in 1805, which secured the Sikh Empire's position in the region.
